questions.stem: In a database, what is a view?
options: A physical copy of a table stored on disk
A virtual representation of a table that encapsulates a query
A backup of the database taken at a point in time
An index that speeds up joins
A stored file containing exported rows
questions.explanation: A view encapsulates a query and acts as a virtual representation of a table; querying it retrieves the combined results without rewriting the query.

questions.stem: Does a database view store its own data?
options: Yes, it stores a permanent copy of the query result
Yes, but only for the most recent query
No, it dynamically fetches data from the underlying tables whenever it is queried
Only when the view joins more than two tables
Only if it is created with an index
questions.explanation: A view itself does not store any data; it dynamically fetches data from the underlying tables whenever it is queried.

questions.stem: When does creating a view become advantageous?
options: When a table has fewer than ten rows
When the database has no primary keys
When a query is run only once
When a query joining several tables is run frequently, such as daily or monthly
When the data must be stored in an external file
questions.explanation: If a join query is run frequently, creating a view lets you execute a simple SELECT on the view instead of rewriting the complex join each time.

questions.stem: How do you retrieve the combined results once a view has been created?
options: By exporting the view to a CSV file
By running REFRESH on the view
By rebuilding the underlying tables
By re-running the original join query manually
By executing a simple SELECT command on the view
questions.explanation: Once the query is encapsulated in a view, a simple SELECT on the view returns the combined results from the underlying tables.

questions.stem: In the EmployeeProfile example, which tables are combined by the view?
options: Employee and Department
Customer and Order
Product and Supplier
Student and Course
Invoice and Payment
questions.explanation: The example view EmployeeProfile selects from Employee and Department where Employee.DeptID = Department.DeptID.

questions.stem: Which SQL statement creates a view?
options: CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT
CREATE VIEW ... AS SELECT
INSERT INTO VIEW
ALTER TABLE ... ADD VIEW
SELECT INTO VIEW
questions.explanation: A view is created with CREATE VIEW followed by the SELECT query it encapsulates, as in CREATE VIEW EmployeeProfile AS SELECT ...

questions.stem: In the EmployeeProfile example, on which condition are the Employee and Department tables joined?
options: Employee.Name = Department.Name
Employee.Salary = Department.Budget
Employee.DeptID = Department.DeptID
Employee.ID = Department.ManagerID
Employee.Location = Department.Location
questions.explanation: The WHERE clause in the example joins the tables on Employee.DeptID = Department.DeptID.

questions.stem: Why is understanding views described as crucial?
options: Because views are the only way to store data securely
Because views replace the need for tables
Because views are required for every SELECT statement
Because they are a foundational concept leading into more advanced topics such as Materialised Views and External Tables
Because views are needed to create primary keys
questions.explanation: Views are a foundational concept whose understanding is needed before moving to more advanced topics such as Materialised Views and External Tables.

questions.stem: What is the main benefit of a view for a frequently needed multi-table result?
options: It doubles the storage used by the tables
It makes the underlying tables read-only
It automatically normalises the tables
It caches the result permanently on disk
It avoids rewriting the complex join query every time the consolidated information is needed
questions.explanation: Querying the view provides the consolidated information without having to rewrite the complex join query each time.

questions.stem: Which statement about a regular database view is NOT correct?
options: A view physically stores a snapshot of the query result
A view can combine data from several tables
A view is queried with a SELECT statement
A view is described as the virtual representation of a table
A view fetches data from the underlying tables at query time
questions.explanation: A regular view does not store any data; it is virtual and fetches from the underlying tables dynamically each time it is queried.
